about: Tool policy for Denisse's brain: what each tool may do, which tools a turn is offered, and the
few phrase lists that still run before the model. Values live here, not in code (AGENTS.md Rule 0).
tools.<name>.side_effect: 'read' may always be called, even when not offered; 'write' only when offered,
never on a complaint turn. checks: run on the CALL's arguments, never on Chuen's wording.
reply_must_mention: after this tool succeeds her reply must match this, else the tool's own sentence
(or fallback_reply) is used -- alone for a 'write' tool, in front of her reply for a 'read' one
(alone for a 'read' one too when must_mention_replaces is true: an invented calendar is not worth keeping).
nothing_must_mention: when the tool ran but did nothing (its result is no evidence: 'nothing was stopped'),
her reply must say so (match this), else the tool's own sentence is used -- a goodbye over 'no session
was running' hides the truth. check kinds: must_match / must_not_match (pattern on the argument),
not_inside_program_folder, not_own_file_name (a path whose file name is one of her own files, {value}),
verified_document_path, known_skill, task_has_subject (the text is nothing but a time, 'Thursday', or filler, 'me'),
unambiguous_time (time_parse has a question about the due phrase; {detail} is that question).
groups: a turn is offered core + every group whose cues match the recent user text (tool_router.py).
cues/study_commands: data for the fast paths that run before the model; edit here, not in code.

checks.refusal: Refused: that command deletes, moves or overwrites his files, and you don't do that -- it can't be undone, and there's no backup to get them back from. Tell him plainly you won't, say why (it's permanent), name the files if that helps, and suggest he does it himself or uses the Recycle Bin.
Refused: no verified document path was supplied -- '{value}' is a document, not an installed app. Use find_files to locate it, then open_application with the full path it returns.
Refused: that's your own program folder, and your settings there are his to edit. Don't write there. Tell him you don't edit your own files, and that he can change them himself.

Refused: '{value}' is one of your own files (your settings, config or code), and you don't edit those -- they're his to change. Don't try another path. Tell him plainly you don't change your own files and he can edit them himself.
No tool needed here. Answer his question directly, in your own words, from what you know.
There's no skill called '{value}'. Don't mention skills or tools to him -- do what he asked with your other tools, or answer directly.

Refused: '{value}' says when, not what -- he didn't say what to remind him of. Ask him, in one short question, what the reminder is for (and which day, if that's unclear too). Don't add anything until he answers.
Refused: '{value}' is ambiguous -- {detail} Ask him that, in one short question, and don't add anything until he answers.

resume_study_session.nothing_must_mention: \b(?:no study|nothing (?:was |is )?(?:running|resumed)|isn'?t running|not running|wasn'?t running|no session|nothing to resume|wasn'?t paused|not paused|there'?s no|wasn'?t (?:one|any))

check_calendar.reply_must_mention: \b(?:can'?t see|can'?t check|can'?t read|can'?t get|can'?t access|no access|don'?t have access|not connected|isn'?t connected|not linked|not hooked up|no calendar|don'?t have (?:a |your )?calendar|no way to see|information about your calendar)\b
check_calendar.fallback_reply: I can't see your calendar -- nothing's connected to one yet. I can check your reminders if that helps.

tutor_explain._note: The study tutor's tools (tutor/chat.py, 2026-11-05). reply_must_mention and fallback_reply are the tutor's name, tutor.json 'name' (tutor/test_teach.py checks the two files agree): a reply that leaves the tutor out gets the tutor introducing itself in front. Reads and model calls; what they record goes to the tutor's own area of the vault. Marking is a write: it closes the open question.
